content.title: Harry Styles explores new sounds in “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally”
content.text: Photo by Sarah Ruzicka | The Triangle “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally” is Harry Styles’s fourth solo album. The album was released on Friday, March 6 and features 12 songs. This release has been highly anticipated by fans as it has been five years since his third album, “Harry’s House,” was released in May of 2022. In “Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally,” Styles takes a new approach to his sound, with this album focusing more on the synth-pop sound, which has not been heard from him before. The lead single “Aperture,” which was released in January, set the tone for the sound of the album. The song features a strong instrumental and is upbeat and danceable. The chorus is catchy and easy to sing along to. With “Aperture” setting the stage for the album, other songs such as “Ready, Steady, Go,” “Season 2 Weight Loss,” and “Pop” also feature the synth-pop sound, with some rock influences in “Ready, Steady, Go.” For those who are fans of Style’s previous work, this sound, while still pop, may take some adjustment, and those who previously have not listened, may find the sound interesting as he branches out from the typical pop sound of the previous singles from other albums. The third track on the album “Ready, Steady, Go,” begins with a sound similar to microphone feedback before the steady bassline kicks in, which keeps the song moving. The chorus of the song features a vocal sound effect that mimics the sound of talking into a radio with a synth in the background. The song is easy to dance to, especially as the pace picks up towards the end of the track.Styles also slows it down for some songs in the album such as “The Waiting Game,” “Coming Up Roses,” and “Paint by Numbers.” “Coming Up Roses” begins with the sound of an orchestra tuning their instruments before a soft piano plays and Styles begins to sing. The ending features an emotional orchestral section that Styles composed himself, embracing the melancholy of the track. The song discusses the potential end of a relationship and wanting to spend a bit more time in the joyful moments before it ends. Discover moreMusical InstrumentsMusic & AudioMusic Reference On the other end of the spectrum, “Dance No More” embraces the disco aspect of the album title. The sound of this song is reminiscent of the song “Le Freak” by Chic. The song has a prominent baseline that starts off the track, sounding like something one would hear in a club. As the title suggests, the song is danceable and fun, with a modern spin on the disco genre. The album ends with “Carla’s Song,” which leaves the listener on a high note with the lyrics “It’s all waiting there for you.” The song provides an introspective experience, with a happy and encouraging sound, a catchy and introspective tune to leave the listener with.
